verdict.rationale: Capacities documents its own REST API with a TypeScript SDK (@capacities/api), an OpenAPI 3.0 spec, an interactive reference with try-it, SDK samples on its developer portal, and MCP-based custom app integration. This lets developers build external integrations. There is no evidence of an in-app plugin or extension system that runs inside Capacities, and the Beta API generation is deprecated as of September 1, 2026. missing for 10: an in-app plugin/extension runtime and API, plugin-specific samples and docs, independent or hands-on corroboration of the SDK.

support.subject: As a developer, I can build my own plugins against a documented extension API/SDK with samples and developer docs

citations.quote: Install the Capacities TypeScript SDK: npm install @capacities/api
Interactive OpenAPI specification with every endpoint, schema, rate limit, and TypeScript SDK sample
The Capacities REST API gives you programmatic access to a workspace space — read and write objects, properties, block content, daily notes, and more.
Build your own app, agent, or bot and integrate it with a Capacities space by implementing a custom MCP client using the Model Context Protocol (MCP) open standard.
